Quantum Harness · Challenge 122
EXPLORATORY RESULT

Learning-Induced Metal-Insulator Transition

Exploratory DIII monitored-Majorana study with an XY-line validation gate

Team 卧龙凤雏

We reproduce the known XY-line learning transition, then test a generic symmetry-class-DIII measurement cut with Born-sampled Gaussian Majorana trajectories. The report explains the mapping, algorithms, parameters, finite-size analysis, anisotropy calibration, uncertainty, and strict exploratory claim gates.

Section 01

Executive result and scope

Exploratory status

The frozen status is xy_reproduced_diii_inconclusive. The directly fitted universal candidate is c_eff α=0.349033; α is not stable, so no standalone c_eff is published.

Section 02

Basic concepts: monitoring and phases

Repeated quantum measurements can either preserve extended Majorana correlations or localize them. The metal-insulator distinction is diagnosed from size trends, entanglement-arc model weights, correlations, and record free energy rather than from one smooth curve.

σ(θ,φ)=sinθ cosφ X + sinθ sinφ Y + cosθ Z

The two angles define the physical single-qubit measurement axis.

Section 03

Surface-code mapping and effective couplings

The surface-code Born tensor network maps to alternating Gaussian measurements and rotations. The real coupling controls information gain; the complex phase controls norm-preserving Majorana rotation.

J(θ)=atanh(cosθ)

This converts the polar measurement angle into a real monitoring strength.

Section 04

Why generic DIII differs from the XY class-D line

The XY line has a special class-D block decomposition. Moving to θ=0.45π with nonzero azimuth removes that decomposition and realizes the generic DIII cut targeted by the open challenge.

Section 05

Gaussian covariance implementation

Rust evolves a real antisymmetric 2L×2L covariance matrix. Rational measurement updates and orthogonal rotations preserve purity analytically; after each period, an orthogonal polar projection removes accumulated roundoff in Γ² = −I. Entropy follows from duplicated singular values of restricted covariance matrices.

Γ′ = R Γ Rᵀ

Every unitary Majorana gate acts by congruence on the covariance matrix.

Section 06

Conditional Born sampling and the IID negative control

Xoshiro256++ draws conditional Born outcomes. The Rao-Blackwellized binary entropy is accumulated before each draw. Unbiased IID signs are a deliberately nonphysical diagnostic and never enter physical summaries.

Section 09

Reproduction of the known XY transition

The XY scan is a validation gate: its finite-size bracket must overlap the declared reference window before any generic-DIII claim is considered.

Section 10

Exploratory generic-DIII phase evidence

The generic scan compares area, logarithmic, squared-logarithmic, and Page-augmented arc models across widths. A transition bracket requires persistent opposite phase evidence on adjacent angles.

Section 11

Casimir amplitude and finite-size correction

γ₁(L)=f∞L−π(c_eff α)/(6L)+a/L³

The coefficient of 1/L is the directly observed product c_eff α; the L^-3 term absorbs leading finite-size drift.

Section 12

Spatial-temporal anisotropy calibration

Spatial parity correlations determine Δ, while the leading temporal Lyapunov gap determines α. Window changes and block deletions must agree before dividing the Casimir amplitude by α.

α=gL/(2πΔ)

This calibration makes the spacetime conversion explicit instead of assuming isotropy.

Section 13

Dual effective-central-charge fits and cross-validation

Exploratory number versus universal constant

All finite exploratory estimates are displayed with intervals and failed gates. Only a bracketed transition, stable fits and anisotropy, sufficient streams and blocks, and estimator agreement can promote the value to candidate status.

S(ℓ,L)=b+(c_eff^S(L)/3) log[(L/π) sin(πℓ/L)]+q cos(2πℓ/L)/L²

The coefficient of the periodic chord-length logarithm defines c_eff^S(L); the central interval suppresses endpoint effects and the cosine term absorbs the leading oscillatory correction.

The entanglement estimate is extrapolated linearly in 1/L². Independently, the Casimir fit measures c_eff α and the Lyapunov/spatial calibration determines α. Their agreement is tested after fitting and is never imposed.

Section 14

Uncertainty, sensitivity, and claim boundary

Uncertainty is hierarchical: streams are resampled first and complete blocks second. Sensitivity checks change minimum width, corrections, phase brackets, correlation windows, and Lyapunov block deletions.

Claim boundary

This is an exploratory finite-size result, not a final universal constant. Finite estimates remain visible with uncertainty intervals and failed gates; only results passing every gate are labeled candidates.
